summary: A Rust command-line tool built as one binary, with clap commands, TOML settings, coded errors and human or JSON output.
description: Write a Rust utility with clap subcommands and typed settings layered from defaults, TOML files, environment variables and flags. Each failure has a code, a fix suggestion and an exit status, printed as text or as JSON. Strict clippy lints, rustfmt and cargo-deny checks are set up, and tests run the built binary. The shipped config show command is the example to copy; your tool's own commands and any release packaging are still yours to add.
seoDescription: A Rust CLI recipe with clap subcommands, layered TOML configuration, coded errors with exit statuses, JSON output and binary tests.

projectExamples.title: Log file summarizer
projectExamples.description: Add a command that reads log files and prints counts per level, as a table for people or JSON for scripts. Reuse the settings layers for default paths.

projectExamples.title: Repository policy checker
projectExamples.description: Add commands that check a repository against rules kept in a TOML file and exit nonzero on a violation, so CI can run the tool.

plain.whatItIs: A starter for a terminal program written in the Rust language, compiled into one file that runs without anything else installed.
goodAt: Commands that read settings from files, environment variables and flags
Output for people to read, or in a structured form scripts can parse
Error messages with a code, a fix and a distinct exit status
notGoodAt: Full-screen terminal screens with menus and panels; that needs a terminal interface stack.
Graphical apps with windows and buttons; choose a web or desktop stack.
